newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sentences two Islamist militants to death.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sentences two Islamist militants to death.

text.p: An Egyptian state security court on Monday sentenced in absentia two Moslem militants to death for killing a police major-general and his two assistants in a southern Egyptian village three years ago.

Judge Ismail Hamed of the Supreme State Security Court sentenced fugitives Anwar Hamed Abbas and Ahmed Abdel Wahab Ahmed Khalil on charges that include belonging to the country's largest militant group, the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), which is fighting to overthrow the government.
The two militants are on the run. They were also charged with possessing unlicensed weapons and receiving illegal funding.
The judge has postponed sentencing the remaining 13 militants charged in the case to October 31. One of the 13 is also on the run.

The court said the two gunmen had killed Major General Mohammed Abdel Latif el-Ghobashi, assistant security chief for the southern Qena province, while he was leaving his house in Nag Hammadi, some 450 km (280 miles) south of Cairo.
The militants also shot dead Ghobashi's guard and driver, policemen Mohammed Sayed and Nasser Mahmoud.
Since 1992, Moslem militant groups have been fighting a bloody battle to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state.
They have targetted policemen and officials as symbols of the government but they have also hit Christians and tourists.
Almost 1,000 people have been killed and scores wounded in the political violence.
